educationalGoal: The goal of the program is to provide students with a broad knowledge of koji, the brewing industry, fermented foods, and the fermentation industry, and to make them useful for the future of the brewing and fermentation industries. advice: The purpose of this course is to learn more deeply about "fermentation" from a scientific viewpoint by studying "koji" and "koji mold," which are indispensable to the fermentation industry in Ishikawa. The objective is to learn more about "fermentation" from a scientific viewpoint by studying "koji" and "koji mold," which are essential to the fermentation industry in Ishikawa. Koji has long been used in traditional Japanese foods. Especially in Ishikawa, koji is used not only for sake, soy sauce, miso, and vinegar, but also for kabura-zushi. In particular, in Ishikawa, koji is used not only for sake, soy sauce, miso, vinegar, and sushi, but also for kabura-zushi, and is very familiar to people in other parts of Japan. However, it is not well known that koji is a "national fungus," and that it is used to make kabura-zushi, a type of sushi. However, it is not well known that the koji mold is "Kokugun" or that Dr. Jokichi Takamine, a great man from Okayama and Kanazawa, produced "Takadiastase" using fusuma koji mold. The "national The goal of this course is to learn about koji, a "national fungus," and "koji" made with koji, to trace the footsteps of a great local man, and to gain a deeper understanding of the fermentation industry in Japan and Ishikawa. The goal is to gain a deep understanding of the fermentation industry in Japan and Ishikawa.
requiredKnowledge: The course requires knowledge of Japanese language (Japanese literature and classics), Japanese history, world history, chemistry, and biology at the level of a high school graduate, as well as extensive knowledge of biology, molecular biology, genetics, etc. at the first or second year university level.

activityGoals.body: To be able to explain the mechanism of "koji mold" from historical and scientific viewpoints.
To be able to explain the mechanism of "koji mold" from the viewpoint of molecular biology and genetics.
To be able to explain the mechanism of "fermentation" from a biochemical point of view.
